name: sweet potato galette
instructions:
This recipe wants to be a GALETTE. It started as a vegetable pot pie (ATK's Vegetable Pot Pie scaffold — see the POT-PIE ERA reference log in notes) and hit a structural dead end on the gravy; the galette format solves it by having NO GRAVY AT ALL — braise the vegetables in chicken stock for flavor, DISCARD the stock, and bind with greek yogurt instead.

=== THE GALETTE BUILD (SO FAR) ===

VEGETABLES: onions, sweet potato, and turnips + garlic are in. SWISS CHARD is in too — LEAVES, not stems. GINGER IS OUT (pot-pie-era spice; see notes).

CRUST: definitely wants a WHOLE WHEAT crust — the America's Test Kitchen whole wheat galette crust with white vinegar is perfect (recipe to be transcribed; see notes).

PROCEDURE:
1. SAUTÉ the onions and garlic.
2. BRAISE the vegetables in CHICKEN STOCK until soft — then DISCARD the stock. (The stock is a flavoring medium, not a gravy — see notes.)
3. BIND with GREEK YOGURT and add DRIED DILL and ALEPPO PEPPER to the filling before baking.
4. LEMON JUICE for brightness — leave out the lemon zest.
5. Assemble in the galette format and bake. Crust: the ATK whole wheat galette crust (white vinegar) once transcribed; [[savory-pie-crust]] is the stand-in until then.
notes:
=== WHY A GALETTE — THE STOCK/GRAVY DEAD END ===

I can see why ATK opted for vegetable broth: it's LIGHT, so the vegetables themselves shine — unlike chicken/beef/dark veggie stock, where the stock dominates the vegetables. HOWEVER, vegetable broth makes a very awkward GRAVY. Experiments with the other stocks just turned into suboptimal chicken/beef pot pies where the veggies don't shine. ATK probably uses parmesan and a smaller amount of stock to help deal with this issue — but I think they're SWALLOWING A SPIDER TO CATCH A FLY.

THE GALETTE SOLUTION: keep the stock's flavor benefit but drop the gravy problem entirely — braise the vegetables in chicken stock until soft, then DISCARD the stock. The chicken stock seasons the vegetables without dominating the dish, and the binding job moves to greek yogurt.

=== THE BINDER — GREEK YOGURT (CHEESES TO TRY) ===

Greek yogurt binds the braised vegetables before baking, with DRIED DILL mixed in. WANT TO TRY: cheese binders — CREAM CHEESE, MONTERREY JACK, PARMESAN — in addition to the yogurt.

ALSO WANT TO EXPERIMENT WITH: FETA / GOAT CHEESE CRUMBLES, and WALNUTS / CHESTNUTS.

=== WANT TO TRY — PORK VARIANT (TURNIP OUT) ===

Pork in this, with the TURNIP REMOVED for it. PROCESSED PORK is probably the best, but minced PORK SHOULDER could work too.

=== LEMON JUICE, NO ZEST ===

Lemon juice for brightness. Leave out the lemon zest.

=== CHARD IN (LEAVES), GINGER OUT ===

SWISS CHARD is in — the LEAVES, not the stems. (The inverse of [[southern-chickpea-soup]], where the stalks are the point.) GINGER IS OUT — the pot-pie era's lemon+ginger+smoked-paprika profile doesn't carry into the galette; the build is dill-forward instead. Smoked paprika and porcini powder are simply dropped.

=== MUSHROOMS OUT — NOT CLASHING, JUST NO ROOM ===

Mushrooms are out as well: not enough space in the galette, and mushrooms are in too many savory pies already. They're NOT clashing — just not in this one.

=== ALEPPO PEPPER — PRIMARY, IN THE FILLING ===

Ottolenghi puts chili peppers in his sweet potato galettes, and the aleppo experiment confirmed it: ALEPPO PEPPER IN THE FILLING before it goes in the oven DOES A LOT. Primary. (The original idea was a chili-butter finish per the turkish yogurt + dill + chili trio — çılbır logic — but the in-filling placement is the tested one. Fresno judged too sweet against the sweet potato; fresh serrano baked on top is the Ottolenghi-faithful alternative if wanted.)

=== OPEN QUESTION — MAYBE THERE ARE TWO PIES HERE ===

The turnips and chard genuinely pair well with the sweet potato — ATK got that right. But the seasoning direction (yogurt/dill/aleppo) and the vegetable trio may want different dishes: (A) a minimal turkish-leaning sweet potato galette where the sweet potato stars, and (B) the three-vegetable root pie the ATK stack proved. Undecided — cook the current all-in build first and see if it feels crowded.

=== BAKE — 400°F, EGG WASH ADDED MIDWAY ===

Something that worked well: bake at 400°F to quickly settle the galette dough, then take it out and add the EGG WASH MIDWAY through — and keep going at 400°F. (Related lesson from [[artisan-french-bread]]: glazes applied from the start cause undercooking; midway application sidesteps that.)

=== CRUST — ATK WHOLE WHEAT GALETTE CRUST (WHITE VINEGAR) ===

This definitely wants a WHOLE WHEAT crust: the America's Test Kitchen whole wheat galette crust with white vinegar is perfect. Recipe to be found and transcribed — until then [[savory-pie-crust]] stands in.

=== POT-PIE ERA — REFERENCE LOG (READ-ONLY) ===

The recipe's previous life as 'turnip yam pie' — a modified ATK Vegetable Pot Pie (bouillon stock instead of vegetable broth, porcini powder instead of parmesan, lemon + ginger + smoked paprika profile, cremini mushrooms + swiss chard in the filling, pie crust or panko top). Cooked successfully several times ('excellent' in that era) but the gravy problem above eventually ended the format. Lessons from that arc, preserved:

- STOCK vs VEGETABLES IS A REAL TRADEOFF: bouillon/chicken made a better gravy than ATK's vegetable broth but pulled the dish toward being a (suboptimal) chicken pot pie — stock strength and vegetable-forwardness fight each other in a gravy format. This is the tension the galette resolves.
- GARDEN VEGETABLE BOUILLON TURNS GRAVY MOSSY GREEN: tasted fine, looked wrong once the roux thickened it. (Gravy-specific lesson; moot in the galette but worth remembering for any roux dish.)
- TURNIPS + SWEET POTATOES are the identity pair — earthy-bitter root + sweet/savory counterweight. Carried into the galette.
- SEASONING PROFILE (pot-pie era): lemon + ginger + smoked paprika, with GINGER AND SMOKED PAPRIKA SAUTÉED AT THE START (fresh ginger added late reads indian — wrong register) and LEMON ADDED LATE. Failure mode: too much lemon/ginger — the sauce reduces in the oven and concentrates both; season under, let the oven concentrate. Decided: this spice profile does NOT carry into the galette — ginger is out, and the build is dill-forward instead.
- PORCINI POWDER OVER PARMESAN worked as the umami move in the gravy (the good version of the glutamate-additions pattern — extended the mushrooms rather than substituting for real ingredients).
- DON'T CHICKEN OUT ON SWISS CHARD quantities — greens wilt to a third of their raw volume.
- ATK'S VEGETABLE REJECTIONS: no asparagus, no leeks — they turn army-green and overcook in a long covered bake.
- PANKO OVER REGULAR BREADCRUMBS for a crumb-top variation — larger flakes crisp; regular crumbs pack down soggy against a wet filling.
- CRUST VENTING (pot format): cut vents while the dough is flat, before it goes on.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[atk-vegetable-pot-pie]]: ATK's original, by the book.
- [[savory-pie-crust]]: the dough.
- [[braised-turnips]]: the turnip register elsewhere.
- [[southern-chickpea-soup]]: the other chicken-stock-as-flavoring-medium dish (there the stock stays; here it's discarded).
original_chef: Mine — descended from America's Test Kitchen's Vegetable Pot Pie (the pot-pie era is preserved as a read-only reference log in notes).
